title: Result Unwrap or Default
story: Your app reads a configuration value from a file. If the file is corrupted, you fall back to a safe default. You don't need a full crash report — you just need to keep running with plan B.
why: Result's .unwrap_or(default) gives you a quick fallback value when you don't need detailed error handling — perfect for configs, defaults, and non-critical operations.
analogy: .unwrap_or on Result is like having a spare tire — if your main tire blows (Err), you don't call a tow truck; you just put on the spare and keep driving.
try_it: Modify fetch_score to return different error messages (e.g., "Player not found" vs "Score unavailable"). Does .unwrap_or care about the error message? When would you switch to match instead?
tips: .unwrap_or on Result works identically to Option — success gives the value, error gives the default
Use .unwrap_or at the last step before displaying to users — keep Results inside your logic chain
The default in .unwrap_or is always evaluated, even for Ok — for expensive defaults, use match
common_mistakes: Using .unwrap_or when you actually need to know what the error was — that information is silently discarded
Providing a default of the wrong type — `result_int.unwrap_or("hello")` won't compile
Assuming .unwrap_or somehow retries or fixes the error — it just returns the default, the error is gone
